cultivar: Local Zaoyazhong and Zhongliuye; Lanxiang No. 1
processing: Fresh leaf is spread, lightly sun-withered, rested and tossed to raise the aroma, then fixed, rolled and baked over charcoal in two rounds with light pressing to shape it. Accounts differ on how much of the fixing is done in the pan.
harvest_season: Spring, one bud with two young leaves; the top grade uses tender shoots of about 3 cm.
appearance_dry: Emerald, even, downy leaf in a slim, flattish form compared to embroidery scissors.
taste_profile: Fresh, mellow and smooth with a sweet aftertaste and a strong orchid-like fragrance, holding up over several steeps.

brewing.notes: Use a glass or gaiwan and do not cover it for long; the orchid note dulls under a closed lid with water too hot.

vintage_note: Sold as a spring tea of the current year, by grade: the Jingxian Lanxiang local standard sets special and first grades. Drink it within the year, as the orchid aroma is the first thing to fade.
description:
Tingxi Lanxiang comes from Tingxi township in Jingxian county in southern Anhui. It is a young tea, and its aim is in the name: lanxiang means orchid fragrance.

The method borrows a little of what aroma-driven teas do. The leaf is spread and lightly withered in the sun, then rested and tossed several times before fixing, rolling and two rounds of charcoal baking. Light pressing gives it the slim shape often compared to embroidery scissors.

Expect a bright, tender green cup with a clear orchid note, a mellow body and a sweet finish. It takes several steeps better than many bud greens. Most mistakes come from very hot water or a closed lid, both of which dull the aroma.

It is sold by spring harvest and grade. The geographical standard for Jingxian Lanxiang covers a set of villages in Tingxi, so ask for the village and the picking date. Prize lists are common in its marketing and tell you less than a fresh sample does.

Neighbouring Lanhua teas from the Dabie Mountains are often grouped with it, though Tingxi lies on an offshoot of the Huangshan range. Tasting one beside Shucheng Xiaolanhua is a good way to see the difference.
history:
Tingxi Lanxiang is a modern tea: it was created in 1989 under the tea scholar Chen Chuan, who is credited with naming it.

It gained provincial famous tea status in 1992 and won national awards through the 1990s. Later work selected local plants into lines such as Lanxiang No. 1, a Jingxian Lanxiang standard was issued in 2013, and Tingxi has held a picking festival since 2003.
sources_note: Accounts differ between flat-straight and scissor-shaped description, and on pan or bake fixing.
